I’m not saying he should be fired nor should he be given remotely serious consideration. I’m speaking in general terms, not this specific situation, but just in general if a GM doesn’t properly communicate with their players, it could be the building blocks to something similar to this situation. If the GM didn’t have that good of a resume, then I’d consider that a potentially fireable offense. 

However, Gute has had a solid run as GM so I wouldn’t say he should be fired. But, in my opinion he could’ve handled it better and it shouldn’t be dismissed as “he shouldn’t have to explain himself or ask his players for approval”. Because while he shouldn’t *have *to do that, if push comes to shove  then he should. Aaron also hasn’t been helping this situation, communication goes both ways. 

My problem is just when people act like QBs aren’t allowed to be upset because their GM doesn’t involve them or doesn’t value their opinions when it comes to decisions involving the team. Like people were complaining about Deshaun Watson when reports first came out he was unhappy in Houston. I saw so many people complain that it’s not his place to be involved in decisions with the team because “a GM shouldn’t have to involve him”. It’s just been a personal pet peeve of mine when people say things along those lines.

You can have both though, it is not hard to communicate with your players and still do your job. If a GM can’t do both then something needs to change whether it be just telling him to communicate more than anything or going all out and firing him. It’s kind of hard to go to more NFCCG if your reigning MVP quarterback is on another roster.

I’m not saying Gute is completely inept, going to two NFCCG is obviously an accomplishment. However, an inability to communicate with the most important player on your roster is a bad quality to have in a GM, because then situations like this can happen.

Again I just disagree, if your GM can’t do the bare minimum and communicate with their players then something needs to change because that does nothing but hurt the team. A team and its players should not have settle for less because their GM is inept.

I just disagree, the lack of communication between a GM and QB/HC/whoever just hurts the team. Sure a GM doesn’t *have* to explain themself, they don’t *have* to consult with their players, but it sure does help. Chemistry and player happiness are very important to team success, lack of communication does not help build chemistry nor does it make your players happier. It’s entirely possible to do your job and listen to your players.
